Cardinal directions are the four main points of a compass: north, south, east, and west. These directions are used in navigation and geography to describe location and orientation. North points towards the North Pole, south towards the South Pole, east towards where the sun rises, and west towards where the sun sets.

To randomly choose a direction, you could use a six-sided die. You would assign each face a corresponding direction: for example, 1 could be north, 2 could be east, 3 could be south, and 4 could be west. The remaining two numbers could be rerolls if they come up. You roll the die and, based on the result, follow the assigned direction. This method provides a simple, chance-based way of selecting one of the four cardinal directions without bias.
